newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index up 0.3 pct at 293.34.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index up 0.3 pct at 293.34.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars, was up 0.3 percent at 293.34 at the start of play on Tuesday.
Latin America edged up 0.3 percent day-on-day to 537.00, Asia was up 0.3 percent at 250.34, while Europe, the Middle East and Africa were up 0.4 percent at 133.91.
Over the year to date, the index was up 6.4 percent, with Latin America up 13.8 percent, Asia up 7.8 percent, but Europe, the Middle East and Africa down 5.5 percent overall.
The IFC composite index touched a 1996 high of 308.77 on July 4, up from the year's 275.79 low, recorded on January 1.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index, also denominated in dollars, was up 0.32 percent day-on-day at 159.58 at 1000 GMT, and up 7.96 percent over the year to date.
The year's high was 165.948, reached on July 3. It touched the year's 148.85 low on January 2.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns from some 20 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.08 percent to 124.66 by the start of trade on Tuesday. It gained 14.81 percent over the year.

By region, Latin America was up 0.15 percent at 102.30, Asia rose 0.08 to 131.26 and East Europe was flat at 162.77. Over the year to date, Latin America was up 31.05 percent, Asia up 8.99 percent, and East Europe was up 17.58 percent.
